statement: The two ramified points in the genus-two test are separated — Let $C/\mathbb F_3$ be the smooth projective model of \[ y^3-y=x+x^{-1}, \] and let $P,Q$ be its rational points over $x=0,\infty$, respectively. Their point sections in the geometrically prime-to-three fundamental group are not geometrically conjugate. This remains true after every finite extension of $\mathbb F_3$. In particular their decomposition groups are not conjugate-commensurate. We construct a finite \emph{\'etale} cover of $C_{\mathbb F_{27}}$, with geometric monodromy of order prime to three, having a rational point over $P$ and none over $Q$. Thus this genus-two test is decided positively, although the general higher-genus assertion retained in B9 is not a consequence of this computation.
depends_on: B7–B8 Kummer and section lifting; explicit quadratic cover and norm identities; Milne AV II Theorem1.1 and III Theorem11.1 for the numerical degree

depends_on_doubtful_reading: none; explicit test and exact covers do not depend on transcription ambiguity
notes: The original F3 genus2 test is resolved, including all finite constant extensions. An étale2 cover gives one lift with elliptic image of exact order5 and the other with Jacobian difference of exact order6. A prime-to3 Lang quotient yields a concrete finite étale cover of degree640 over F27, geometrically prime-to3, with a rational point over P and none over Q. The general higher-genus assertion of B9 remains open. Code F7_test.py passes34 exact checks.

statement: An elliptic quotient separates the genus-two quintic test — Let $C/\mathbb F_5$ be the smooth projective curve \[ y^2=x^5+(x^2+1)^2, \qquad P=(0,1),\quad Q=\infty. \] Although $[P-Q]$ has exact order five in $J_C$, the points $P,Q$ give distinct geometrically prime-to-five point-section classes over every finite extension of $\mathbb F_5$. There is a finite \emph{\'etale} cover of degree $16$ over $\mathbb F_5$, with geometric monodromy of order prime to five, having a rational point above $P$ and none above $Q$.
depends_on: B7–B8 prime-to-p Kummer and fixed-fibre section lifting; B14 finite-cover comparison; explicit unramified quadratic cover and elliptic Lang isogeny
manuscript_passages: cote149; section1; manuscript p17; scans35–36; F7 covering argument
notes: The F5 genus2 quintic test is resolved over every finite constant extension. Étale2 cover has an elliptic quotient with exactly8 F5-points; both Q-lifts have nonzero2-primary elliptic norm differences from Pprime. The pullback of the elliptic Lang cover gives an actual degree16 cover over F5 with geometrically prime-to5 monodromy, a rational point above P and none above Q. F7_test5.py passes20 exact checks. The universal higher-genus B9 remains unresolved.
